Fantastic talks #SugarRushwithScience at the Aug 2026 edition last week, delving into 2 deep science concepts in biology and the potential they unlock for therapeutics in modern medicine:

1) Circular RNA-based vaccines and biologics as the next-generation in mRNA biologics technology beyond the COVID-19 vaccine.  
2) Role of physical confinement, stiffness and other physical control parameters in affecting cell cycles, biological behaviour and cellular state.

Here's a quick recap of the key takeaways for those who missed it!

Dr. Monalisa Chatterji, Co-Founder, C-CAMP-supported startup Sekkei Bio Private Limited, spoke about their work on AI-driven design and development of circular RNA biologics and their current efforts with HER2/neu circular RNA vaccines as a cutting-edge cancer immunotherapeutic.

Monalisa shared Sekkei's innovation journey with their target-agnostic AI drug discovery engine and their motivations in exploring circular RNA-based biologics as their first thrust area. She highlighted the twin advantages of circRNA with longer-lasting protein expression conferring long-term immune function and better stability compared to traditional linear mRNA, such as the COVID-19 vaccines. 

Dr. Tapomoy Bhattacharjee, Faculty, National Centre for Biological Sciences (NCBS), spoke of different types of hydrogels and their physical properties that can give a selective advantage to certain shapes of cells or orientation or modify biochemistry or delay the life cycle. He explained how his lab has sculpted 3D cultures of cells and studied how they respond to stiffness or hypoxia [tuning of oxygen capability]. 

He also mentioned that tailor-made culture media for drug expression can enable faster and improved in vivo testing of drug candidates, thereby accelerating preclinical trials, a key gap in broken therapeutics pipelines.

Building evidence-driven healthcare innovation for India

Society for Innovation & Entrepreneurship - SINE IIT Bombay hosted an HTA Workshop on 7 August 2026, in collaboration with DHR, HTAIn, and ICMR–NIRRWoH, bringing together ~100 startups, innovators, researchers, and healthcare stakeholders online and in person.

The workshop covered HTA fundamentals, evidence and data requirements, study parameters, and decision-making, with practical case studies helping startups apply these concepts to their technologies.

The session highlighted the importance of integrating HTA and evidence generation early to help startups navigate the path from technology development to healthcare adoption and impact.

A special thanks to Dr. Shankar Prinja for his insightful session on “AI in Healthcare Technology Assessment: Opportunities and Challenges.”

We sincerely thank Dr. Beena Joshi, Dr. Oshima Sachin, Dr. Yogesh Gurav, Dr. Manju Sengar and her team, along with all the speakers - Dr. Sivasubramaniam S A, Dr.varun kashyap, Dr. Asim, and Ms. Tejal R Varekar for sharing their valuable insights and making the workshop a meaningful learning experience. 

We also thank all the participants for their enthusiastic participation and valuable contributions. 

A special thanks to Dr. Balu Venugopal for initiating this important engagement.

We look forward to continued engagement through follow-up sessions and startup-specific HTA interactions, helping innovators build evidence-driven technologies ready for assessment and adoption.
